newsitem.title: UK: Heat, diesel demand lifts NWE gas oil premiums.
newsitem.headline: Heat, diesel demand lifts NWE gas oil premiums.

text.p: Strengthening demand for heating oil and low sulphur diesel gave a gentle lift to NWE gas oil cargo premiums in livelier business on Tuesday, traders said.
A weaker U.S. heating oil market and canal traffic delays due to ice depressed benchmark Jan IPE by $2.50 to $229.50 a tonne and Feb IPE by $2.25 to $226.25.

But growing demand pushed cargoes around 50 cents higher. A 10,000 tonne German DIN gas oil cargo traded at Feb IPE +$7.75 for January 15, while a 10,000 tonne Russian traded into Kiel for arrival by Wednesday at Jan +$7/8. German heating sold in tank in Hamburg at Feb IPE +$9.75.
A refinery grade heating oil cargo was offered later at Feb IPE +$9.
Low sulphur diesel cargo demand revived, bid for January 20-30 at Feb IPE +$13 and offered at Feb IPE +$14 basis Le Havre. German grade was bid at Feb IPE+$12.
In barges, prompt refinery grade heating oil went steady to slightly firmer at Jan IPE +$3 fob Rotterdam and +$3.50 fob Antwerp. Second half January went for Jan IPE +$2.50 fob ARA.
Iced-up canals in inland German continued to depress levels of trade to end-users
